text: Do you remember the stories I read to you a little while ago? I want you to tell me the stories again. Tell me everything that you can remember about the first story. Start at the beginning. Do you need a hint about the story topic?
The story was about a woman who was robbed.
Now tell me everything that you can remember about the first story.
Now tell me everything that you can remember about the second story. Start at the beginning.  Do you need a hint about the story topic?
The story was about a weather bulletin
Now tell me everything that you can remember about the second story.
Do you have anything else to add?
I am going to ask you some questions about the first story. If you are not sure of the answers, give your best guess.
Was the woman’s name Diana Thompson?
Was the story setting in South Boston?
Was the woman a cook?
Did she work at a restaurant?
Did she have four children?
Were the children teenagers?
Did the robbery take place on sixth street?
Did the woman report being robbed two nights before?
Did she report robbery at the police station?
Was the woman robbed of 75 dollars?
Did the family go without food for four days?
Was the rent due?
Did the police catch the thief?
Did the police feel sorry for the woman?
Did the police take up a collection?
Now, I am going to ask you some questions about the second story. If you are not sure of the answers, give your best guess.
Was the man’s name Joe Garcia?
Was it Sunday evening?
Was it 6:00PM?
Was the story setting in Seattle?
Was Joe dressing to go out?
Was Joe watching television?
Was the program interrupted?
Was the storm expected to move into the area on Tuesday?
Was the storm expected to stay in the area through the night?
Was the temperature predicted to drop 30 degrees?
Did the announcer predict 10 inches of rain?
Did the announcer warn of possible flooding?
Did the announcer warn that it could hail?
Did Joe decide to stay home?
Did Joe sit down to watch a sports program?
The experiment is now complete. Thank you for participating!
